discovery: The optical lattice clock: magic-wavelength trapping of neutral atoms enabling optical frequency measurement at the 10^-18 level

nominees.name: Hidetoshi Katori
nominees.affiliation: University of Tokyo and RIKEN, Japan

nominees.name: Jun Ye
nominees.affiliation: JILA, NIST and University of Colorado Boulder, USA

subfield: Atomic, molecular and optical physics / precision measurement
motivation: Katori proposed and first demonstrated the optical lattice clock, trapping neutral atoms in a light field tuned to a 'magic' wavelength so that the clock transition is unperturbed by the trap. This combined the large atom numbers of neutral ensembles with the Lamb-Dicke confinement of trapped ions. Ye developed the strontium lattice clock into the most precise instrument ever built, achieving systematic uncertainties and stabilities near 10^-18, controlling atomic interactions and resolving the gravitational redshift across a millimetre-scale sample. Together they turned atomic spectroscopy into a tool that tests general relativity in the laboratory, searches for variation of fundamental constants and dark matter, enables relativistic geodesy, and is driving the redefinition of the SI second. This is careful experimental atomic physics at its finest, with consequences far beyond its own field.
